coordinate_convention: X arrays are indexed [column][row]; W is indexed [row][column]; Forrelation arrays are [layer][coordinate]. All indices are zero-based. Paper [m] is mapped by i_paper=i_lean+1. Address bits are ordered h=0,1,...; no integer interpretation or pointer endianness is assumed.

example.A_rule: Every column: h=0 uses forrelation.yes; h=1..39 use forrelation.zero.
example.transcript: QuarticQuery.circuitEval C (A i h), one bit per actual non-input gate. Keep symbolic unless generated from this exact C.
example.pointer_bits: (QuarticQuery.pointerEquiv 2).symm target_row, in Fin 2 coordinate order; show decoded row labels until exact bit order is exported.
example.blank_cells: All pointer and transcript bits false, as in QuarticQuery.dummy.
example.changed_locations: Only X_0[0] and the bits inside B_{0,(1,0,...,0)} can change. Some bits in that cell may remain equal to their blank value.

proof_scale.status: symbolic asymptotic illustration, not timing data
proof_scale.quantifier_order: fix k>=2, choose constants and threshold, then grow m through powers of four

rendering.style: Flat high-contrast mathematical diagram; colour supplements labels and line styles. Keep board position and IDs stable across shots.
rendering.semantic_labels: Always label zero positions with 0 and winner condition with its full words. Dotted borders mean omitted cells, not probability.

limits: The fixed example uses repeated known address inputs, not the hard independent distribution of the lower bound.
m=4 gives L=0, so Proposition 4.2 asymptotics do not assert a useful bound here.
No concrete speedup measurements or wall-clock claims are made.
No actual quantum experiment is represented.
